criteria.criterion: A test shows that a write attempt in the verifier's snapshot (a file edit or a git commit) fails or is denied, and that the snapshot's HEAD and work-tree tree are unchanged afterwards. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: The test a_verifier_write_attempt_is_refused_and_leaves_the_snapshot_unchanged passes, but it returns early when the file write succeeds ('Permission bits do not bind the superuser'), skipping every check on the commit, HEAD and work tree. `ls -lnd crates` shows uid 0 ownership, so the tests most likely ran as root, where the write succeeds and the test checks nothing. The athena-git test a_locked_snapshot_refuses_writes_and_unlocks_again also skips its refusal and HEAD/tree checks as root; it only checks that the write bits were cleared. Inference: I could not run `id`.

criteria.criterion: A test using the fake agent shows a changed snapshot fingerprint after the first verifier run triggers exactly one more verifier invocation on a freshly created snapshot, and that the first verdict is discarded.
criteria.evidence: a_changed_snapshot_discards_the_verdict_and_reruns_once_on_a_fresh_snapshot passed. It asserts started == [false, false]: two runs, and the second snapshot lacks the first run's file. The first verdict ('fail') is replaced by the rerun's Pass, and the job lands. The test with two changed snapshots asserts started.len() == 2, so there is never a third run.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that when the fingerprint changed, the outcome is recorded as a system fault, and the judgment does not contain the 'verifier changed its snapshot' rejection blocker or reject the work.
criteria.evidence: These passed: verify::tests::a_system_fault_is_a_note_and_never_rejects_the_work (verdict Pass, no reasons, one 'System fault' Nit finding), the rerun test (exactly one 'System fault' finding, none containing 'invalidates'), and a_second_changed_snapshot_is_a_system_fault_not_a_rejection_and_is_not_rerun_again (job Failed, not Rejected; reason contains 'system fault'; no Blocker or Major findings).

criteria.criterion: When the snapshot is unchanged, the verifier runs once and the verdict is used as before; existing tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: an_unchanged_snapshot_runs_the_verifier_once_and_uses_its_verdict passed (one run, job Landed, no fault findings). Athena's full cargo test run passed (665 tests).

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test pass on the workspace.
criteria.evidence: Athena reports that cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and cargo test --locked (665 tests) passed on this tree. My targeted test run also passed.

criteria.criterion: In run.rs the snapshot-changed branch near the old line 959 now discards the verdict and reruns once, and verify.rs no longer turns snapshot_changed into a blocker for the work.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: run.rs now loops at most VERIFIER_RUNS = 2 times. On a fingerprint change it clears verdict_output, commands_run and verifier_invocation and builds a fresh snapshot with verifier_snapshot(). In verify.rs, snapshot_changed became system_fault: a Nit finding that adds no reason and is no longer part of the pass condition.

findings.summary: As root, the write-attempt tests check nothing, and the lock does not stop a root verifier.
findings.evidence: `if wrote { return; }` skips all checks when the write succeeds. The build files are owned by uid 0 (`ls -lnd crates`), so the tests most likely ran as root, where the write succeeds. That leaves criterion 1 unproven, and in this environment the lock is not what stops a write. Possible fixes: send the write through the grant's write deny (crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs), drop privileges in the test, or fail outright when running as superuser.

findings.summary: If the budget runs out before the rerun, the job's reason says the snapshot changed twice.
findings.evidence: When check_budget fails on attempt 1, fault_unresolved is set to true. Later, judgment.reasons is replaced with 'system fault: the verifier changed its snapshot twice', which hides the budget failure message. No test covers this path.
findings.location: crates/athena-core/src/run.rs, the verifier loop and the fault_unresolved handling

summary: Fail, on criterion 1. Most of the change does what was asked: the verifier's snapshot is made read-only while the verifier runs. If the snapshot still changes, that verdict is thrown away and the verifier runs once more on a fresh snapshot, and the fault is recorded as a system fault (a Nit finding) rather than a rejection of the work. If the rerun also changes its snapshot, the job ends `failed`, not `rejected`. The 'verifier changed its snapshot' blocker is gone from verify.rs. The five new tests pass (cargo test -p athena-core -- snapshot system_fault), and every changed file is on the deliverables list. But the build files are owned by uid 0, so the tests most likely run as root (I couldn't run `id`; the policy blocks it). Root ignores file permission bits, so the write-attempt test's file write succeeds and the test returns early. It never checks that the write or commit was refused, or that HEAD and the work tree are unchanged; it passes having shown nothing. The athena-git lock test has the same gap; as root it only checks that the write bits were cleared. The cause is real: as root the lock does not stop a verifier from writing, so only the existing grant write deny and the after-run comparison protect the snapshot. A smaller bug: if the budget runs out before the rerun, the job's reason wrongly says the snapshot changed twice.
